reviews.title: Refund denied
reviews.text:
I am requesting that this refund be reviewed based on inaccurate trial timing, rather than as a standard request for a refund after forgetting to cancel.

I downloaded the app and started what was advertised as a 7-day free trial on October 22. I was charged $74.99 for an annual subscription on October 28, before I believed the full seven-day trial period had ended. I canceled the subscription on October 29, which was the seventh day after I started the trial.

When I initially requested a refund, I mistakenly believed that I had simply canceled one day too late. After reviewing the dates, I realized that this is not what happened. My concern is that I was charged for the annual subscription before receiving the full 7-day free trial that was advertised.

I have already had two refund requests denied, but I don’t believe the actual issue—the discrepancy between the advertised 7-day trial and the date I was charged—has been properly reviewed. I am asking for this specific concern to be escalated and reviewed. I canceled the subscription immediately after discovering the charge and am requesting a refund of the $74.99 annual fee.

Thank you for taking another look at the timeline and circumstances of this charge.

reviews.title: No Science of Reading aligned
reviews.text: I pretty disappointed in this app. As a reading specialist I wanted something I could practice with my daughter to help her learn the sounds. Once we got to long o, that made r controlled vowels long o sounds, which are two very different sounds. The high frequency words can be decoded if aligned correctly in the app. This has so much potential but fell short on helping my child with reading. With better alignment to science of reading scope and sequence this app could be extremely beneficial

reviews.title: Lesson code limits my son’s independence
reviews.text:
The “Grownup required” code prevents my son from opening lessons independently. Each time it appears, he needs me to enter the code before he can continue. I have checked the available settings and have not found a way to turn it off.

This makes him dependent on me just to access the lessons and limits how useful this app is for our family. Parents should have the option to disable the lesson code while keeping purchases and account settings protected.

I have contacted support and am waiting for a response. If this restriction cannot be removed, we have paid for an app that does not meet my son’s needs.

reviews.title: Only allows one lesson per day
reviews.text:
I was disappointed with the program because it only allowed my child to complete one lesson per day. She completed the assessment prior to starting, but Lesson 22 was very basic and primarily reviewed words and sounds she already knew. She completed it quickly and was ready to move on to the next lesson.

Unfortunately, the program only allowed her to “review” the following lesson rather than actually complete it. This left her bored and frustrated because she wanted to continue learning at her own pace.

I ultimately cancelled the subscription after the free trial. I think the program could be much more effective if children who demonstrate mastery could progress through lessons without a one-lesson-per-day restriction.

reviews.title: Company is non-responsive
reviews.text: I signed up because it advertised there would be no charge if I cancelled within the first 30 days and I wanted to give it a shot with my 4 year old. She had no interest in the game. It has a lengthy alphabet song that it tries to make you play at every level that she (and I) didn’t like, the activities were extremely basic—they aren’t even games, so it’s not interesting to kids. You’re supposed to move a slider with your finger while saying a letter’s sound out loud. That’s not a game. I completed the information of where my child was at with reading and it didn’t make sense where we were in placement—it was trying to introduce her to each letter and the sound it makes, and we are beyond that, so it’s even more boring for her. I emailed the company twice requesting a refund since we only tried the game for 1 day and I got an automated message saying they’re swamped with emails essentially—probably other parents trying to cancel. Now I have to call my credit card company to request they get involved for a refund. Waste of time.
